name: @autoqai/mcp

tools.name: aqi_connection
tools.description: Single source of truth for connection state. Returns project identity, port, version, capabilities, uptime, the number of paired clients, AND the list of bound tabs (targets). When NO client is paired it also returns pairing instructions the USER must follow manually (do not automate them). Pass probe=true to additionally round-trip a ping over the WebSocket to confirm the socket is live. Call this once at the start instead of separate pairing/status/list-targets/ping calls.

probe.description: When true, also performs a live WebSocket round-trip ("ping") to the paired extension to verify the socket is responsive. Omit for a cheap state read.

target.description: Optional bound-tab selector for the probe round-trip.

tools.name: aqi_page_info
tools.description: Get URL, title, viewport, scroll, content size, UA, ready state.

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

tools.name: aqi_snapshot
tools.description: Capture DOM and accessibility tree of the bound tab.

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

tools.name: aqi_screenshot
tools.description: Capture screenshot. Writes to disk and returns the relative file path. Never returns base64.

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

fullPage.description: Capture the entire scrollable page instead of just the visible viewport.

selector.description: Capture only this element. Omit for the viewport (or whole page with fullPage).

tools.name: aqi_evaluate
tools.description: Evaluate JS to READ DOM/state only — never to act on the page. No el.click(), no dispatchEvent (MouseEvent/KeyboardEvent), no setting input.value: synthetic events miss framework handlers and step tracking, so they silently do nothing. For any mouse/keyboard action use aqi_click / aqi_type / aqi_hover / aqi_select_option / aqi_drag / aqi_press_key. Always supply a short description of what the script inspects.

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

expression.description: JavaScript expression to evaluate in the page.

description.description: Required. Short human-readable explanation of what this script inspects (≤ 15 words), e.g. "Read window.location.href" or "Check if the datepicker is open". Shown to the user in the live run step row.

tools.name: aqi_type

text.description: The text to enter into the element.

mode.description: How to enter the text. "fill" (default) atomically sets the value of an input/textarea/contenteditable — fast and reliable for ordinary fields. "keystrokes" dispatches per-character key events (use for masked inputs, autocompletes, rich editors, or anything with per-keystroke handlers). delayMs/focusFirst only apply in keystrokes mode.

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

tools.name: aqi_wait_for_render
tools.description: Wait until DOM mutations in a subtree go quiet (client-side render settles). Use after aqi_wait_for_network_idle for canvas/chart sizing or virtualized tables that finish a frame after the network call ends.

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

rootSelector.description: Subtree to watch for DOM mutations. Omit to watch document.body.

minStableMs.description: Quiescence window: how long the DOM must stay unchanged. Default 500ms.

tools.name: aqi_get_table_data
tools.description: Read a PREVIEW of a single table (top 25 rows) as headers + row objects for inspecting/asserting one page. The result reports the total row count and whether it was truncated. This is a context-light preview, NOT a full read: to validate or compare an entire table, use aqi_extract_table (+ aqi_compare for two sides) or targeted aqi_assert_* checks — that path is offline, handles thousands of rows, and never floods context.

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

selector.description: CSS selector for the <table> or a container whose first <table> is used.

tools.name: aqi_get_form_fields
tools.description: Read the fields of a single form (labels, types, values, required/disabled/readonly, options, tabs) including ARIA custom controls (combobox, switch, slider, spinbutton, listbox). Use for inspecting/asserting one page. NOTE: when comparing two forms across pages or states, use aqi_extract_form on each side then aqi_compare (offline, no AI tokens, more accurate).

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

selector.description: Container selector. Omit to scan the whole page body.

tools.name: aqi_extract_table
tools.description:
Extract a normalized table snapshot into a comparison artifact (scoped to the run). Resolves rowspan/colspan into a dense grid, captures per-cell visible/hidden/aria/title/alt text, decoration icons, links and form controls, and computed styles, and normalizes values per declared column type. Returns metadata only — never the row data — so it is safe on tables with thousands of rows.

PREFER THIS over aqi_get_table_data when you are comparing two tables across pages/states: extract each side into its own artifactKey, then call aqi_compare. The comparison runs offline (no AI tokens) and is far more accurate than reasoning over raw rows.

Declare columnMappings so headers worded differently on each side ("Total cost" vs "Total Cost in USD") canonicalize to the same key.

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

selector.description: CSS selector for the <table> element or a container whose first <table> is used.

artifactKey.description: Unique key to store this snapshot under, e.g. "old_cashflow_table". Pass it to aqi_compare.

headerMatch.description: Substring (or regex when regex=true) to match the header text. Case-insensitive.

canonical.description: Canonical key for this column. Use the SAME canonical key on both sides so the diff aligns columns.

type.description: Value type for normalization (defaults to text).

tools.name: aqi_extract_form
tools.description: Extract a form snapshot into a comparison artifact: field labels, types, values, required/disabled/readonly flags, help text, placeholders, tab, and group. Detects native inputs, selects, textareas, AND ARIA custom controls (combobox, switch, slider, spinbutton, listbox, radiogroup). PREFER THIS over aqi_get_form_fields when comparing two forms — extract each side then call aqi_compare (offline, no AI tokens).

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

selector.description: Container selector — a form, modal, panel, or scoped region.

artifactKey.description: Unique key to store this snapshot under. Pass it to aqi_compare.

labelMatch.description: Substring to match the field label. Case-insensitive.

canonical.description: Canonical field key. Use the same key on both sides.

tools.name: aqi_extract_chart
tools.description: Extract a chart snapshot by reading aria-labels chart libraries (Highcharts, Chart.js) emit on series points. Captures series names, (x,y) point lists, axis labels, and overlay markers. PREFER THIS over screenshots/aqi_evaluate when comparing two charts — extract each side then call aqi_compare (offline, no AI tokens). Scope the selector to a single mounted chart, not a wrapping card/section/dashboard. Falls back to a warning when the chart uses a non-standard accessibility layer.

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

selector.description: CSS selector for the exact element the chart is mounted into (the container the chart library renders its <svg>/<canvas> into) — NOT a wrapping card/section/dashboard or one spanning several charts. A too-broad selector merges sibling charts into one series set and the diff finds nothing. Scope to one chart at a time.

artifactKey.description: Unique key to store this snapshot under. Pass it to aqi_compare.

tools.name: aqi_extract_section
tools.description: Extract a labelled-value section — metric cards, dt/dd lists, indicator banners — into a comparison artifact. Captures label+value pairs and decoration icons. Extract each side then call aqi_compare (offline, no AI tokens).

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

selector.description: Container selector — metric cards, dt/dd lists, indicator banners.

artifactKey.description: Unique key to store this snapshot under. Pass it to aqi_compare.

tools.name: aqi_extract_style
tools.description: Extract computed CSS properties for an element into a comparison artifact (curated default set: color, font-*, border-*, padding, margin, display, opacity). Extract each side then call aqi_compare (offline). Use when the user asked for visual/style parity.

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

selector.description: Selector for the element whose computed styles to capture.

artifactKey.description: Unique key to store this snapshot under. Pass it to aqi_compare.

properties.description: Override the curated default CSS property set.

tools.name: aqi_compare
tools.description:
Diff two extracted artifacts by key. Pure offline comparison — NO AI tokens — and far more accurate than reasoning over raw data. The artifact type is inferred from the left artifact (or pass kind to force it): the matching engine runs automatically.
- table: title/header mismatches, missing columns, row-count, per-row cell mismatches (visible/hidden/aria/title/alt text, computed styles, links/form controls), decoration mismatches, extra rows, plus a hoverNotice flagging tooltip elements to hover-probe. Options: keyColumns, tolerance, ignoreColumns.
- form: title/tab-label mismatches, missing/extra fields, per-field diffs (label/value/type/required/help text). Options: ignoreFields, ignoreHelpText.
- chart: series missing per side, per-point y-value differences aligned by x, overlay marker differences. Option: tolerance.
- section: item value differences, missing items, title mismatch (items matched by loose label equality).
- style: property-by-property computed-style diff. Option: ignoreProperties.
Record the result as a finding (pass the diffArtifactKey) so the UI can render the full breakdown.

leftArtifactKey.description: Artifact key of the first ("old"/left) side.

rightArtifactKey.description: Artifact key of the second ("new"/right) side.

diffArtifactKey.description: Key to store the structured diff under.

leftLabel.description: Display label for the left side, e.g. "Old UI".

rightLabel.description: Display label for the right side, e.g. "New UI".

kind.description: Artifact type to diff. Optional — when omitted it is inferred from the stored left artifact. Pass it only to force a specific comparator.

keyColumns.description: table only: canonical columns whose combined value identifies a row. Prefer this when rows have a natural id — makes the diff robust to reordering.

tolerance.description: table/chart only: absolute numeric tolerance (currency/number/percent columns, or chart y-values). Default 0.

ignoreColumns.description: table only: canonical columns to skip when diffing values.

ignoreFields.description: form only: canonical field keys to skip.

ignoreHelpText.description: form only: skip help-text comparison. Default false.

ignoreProperties.description: style only: CSS properties to skip.

tools.name: aqi_assert_text
tools.description: Assert an element contains (or exactly equals) the expected text. Records a fail finding when it does not match.

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

nth.description: Zero-based index when the selector matches multiple.

exact.description: If true, requires an exact match. If false (default), checks the element contains the text.

tools.name: aqi_assert_state
tools.description: Assert a boolean element state — visible, enabled, or checked — via the state arg. Records a fail finding when it does not match.

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

nth.description: Zero-based index when the selector matches multiple.

state.description: Which boolean element state to assert: "visible" (is it shown), "enabled" (vs disabled), or "checked" (checkbox/radio/switch).

expected.description: Expected value of the state. Default true (visible / enabled / checked).

tools.name: aqi_assert_value
tools.description: Assert an input/select/textarea has the expected value.

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

nth.description: Zero-based index when the selector matches multiple.

tools.name: aqi_assert_element_has_class
tools.description: Assert an element has (or does not have) a specific CSS class.

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

nth.description: Zero-based index when the selector matches multiple.

className.description: CSS class name to check for.

hasClass.description: Expected: true = element should have the class, false = should not. Default true.

tools.name: aqi_assert_element_count
tools.description: Assert the number of elements matching a selector relates to the expected count by the given operator (eq/gt/gte/lt/lte).

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

tools.name: aqi_assert_style
tools.description: Assert an element's computed CSS property matches an expected value (substring by default).

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

nth.description: Zero-based index when the selector matches multiple.

expected.description: Expected computed value (substring or exact when exact=true).

exact.description: Require exact match instead of substring. Default false.

tools.name: aqi_assert_network_success
tools.description: Assert all captured network requests completed successfully (status < 400 and no failure). Optionally filter by method or by a since timestamp.

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

since.description: Only check requests captured after this epoch-ms timestamp.

tools.name: aqi_assert_no_console_errors
tools.description: Assert there are no error-level console messages (optionally also warnings) captured on the page.

target.description: Bound tab selector. Omit if only one tab is bound.

since.description: Only check messages captured after this epoch-ms timestamp.

includeWarnings.description: Also fail on warnings, not just errors. Default false.

tools.name: aqi_wait_for_user_command
tools.description: Park until the top queue item is available. Returns { kind, runId, item (compact routing summary only), contextFile } — the full brief, bug context, attached screenshots, console/network trails and notes are written to the contextFile (a markdown file under .autoqai/tmp/context/<date>/). READ contextFile first to understand the work; do not expect the full details inline. The agent branches on kind: "testing-task", "bug-report", "testcase-run" (execute stored test cases — read them from .autoqai/testcases/ yourself), or "testcase-generation" (create/update the stored test-case library files on disk). Once handed off the item is no longer queued.

tools.name: aqi_emit_testcases
tools.description: Append test cases to the current run plan. Can be called multiple times during a run. Provide an id per test case for stable referencing.

tools.name: aqi_start_testcase
tools.description: Mark a test case as running. Required before any interactive tool calls that belong to this test case.

tools.name: aqi_finish_testcase
tools.description: Mark a test case finished with a status. Steps recorded between start and finish belong to this test case.

tools.name: aqi_record_finding
tools.description: Append a finding to the current run. Auto-links to the running test case if one is active. Pass isBug=true for real defects (vs test-execution issues). Use this for ANY issue you notice while working — including unrelated alignment/spacing, color-contrast, styling, accessibility or copy problems (type="warning" or "fail", isBug=false for those). Pass screenshotFile with the path returned by a FOCUSED aqi_screenshot of the affected element so the user can see it; the server copies that image into the run so it survives temp cleanup. When the finding describes a comparison result, pass diffArtifactKey (the diffArtifactKey you gave an aqi_compare_* tool) so the manage UI can render the full diff in a bottom sheet.

diffArtifactKey.description: Key of a diff artifact produced by an aqi_compare_* tool. Attaching it lets the manage UI render the full table/chart/form/section/style difference under this finding.

diffSideLabels.description: Display labels for the two compared sides (e.g. { left: "Old UI", right: "New UI" }). Used to label the diff columns in the UI.

tools.name: aqi_job_complete
tools.description: Finalize the current run with a status and optional summary note + token usage. After this call the agent should call aqi_wait_for_user_command for the next item.

tools.name: aqi_get_issue_details
tools.description: Fetch a Jira issue (description, status, assignee, comments, attachments, linked issues) through the paired browser session.

instructions:
AutoQAI MCP server. You drive an already-paired browser via aqi_* tools and surface progress to the user through tool calls only — NOT through chat prose.

STRICT EXECUTION POLICY:
- Between tool calls, emit ZERO text. No prose, no "I'll now…", "Let me…", "Next I'll…", "Done.", "Continuing…", no status updates, no recaps.
- Only sequential tool calls are permitted between aqi_wait_for_user_command and aqi_job_complete. The user sees nothing in the CLI; the UI is driven entirely by aqi_* tool calls.
- The ONLY user-visible surfaces are: aqi_emit_testcases, aqi_start_testcase, aqi_finish_testcase, aqi_record_finding, aqi_job_complete. Anything you would have written as prose belongs in aqi_record_finding instead.
- If the stop flag fires, the very next aqi_* tool short-circuits with a cancellation result. Stop calling tools immediately — do not write a goodbye message.

Loop shape:
aqi_wait_for_user_command -> READ the returned contextFile (and projectContext) -> branch on item.kind -> drive the page via aqi_* tools -> aqi_job_complete -> aqi_wait_for_user_command again.
- aqi_wait_for_user_command returns only a COMPACT item summary plus a contextFile path. The full brief / bug context / attached screenshots / console+network trails / notes live in that file. ALWAYS read contextFile (and any screenshot paths it lists) before acting. Never assume the details are inline.
- testing-task: aqi_emit_testcases first, then PER test case: aqi_start_testcase -> interactive tools (aqi_click / aqi_type / aqi_press_key / aqi_select_option / aqi_hover / aqi_drag / aqi_upload_file / aqi_wait_for_*) -> aqi_record_finding for every observation worth surfacing -> aqi_finish_testcase. After all cases: aqi_job_complete.
- bug-report: this is also a live, user-visible run — the UI shows EVERY browser interaction as a step under a test case, so you MUST declare what you are about to do before doing it. aqi_emit_testcases first (e.g. one case titled "Reproduce <bug>" and, if you apply a fix, another "Verify fix"), then PER case: aqi_start_testcase -> interactive tools to reproduce / validate -> aqi_record_finding (isBug=true on real defects) -> aqi_finish_testcase. Apply code fixes with your editor tools between the reproduce and verify cases. Never run interactive tools outside a started test case. After all cases: aqi_job_complete.
- Always declare your test case with aqi_start_testcase before any interactive tool so each step is attributed to the right case.
- testcase-run: item.selection = { moduleIds, features:[{moduleId,featureId}], testcases:[{moduleId,featureId,testCaseId}] } describing what the user chose. moduleIds run every feature in that module; features run every case in that feature; testcases run ONLY those specific case ids within their feature. DO NOT expect the cases inline — read them from disk so context stays small. Read contextFile for the exact selection breakdown and the on-disk layout, then open ONLY the feature files you need, one at a time. Then aqi_emit_testcases (title = feature name + the case description) and run each like a testing-task (aqi_start_testcase -> interactive tools -> aqi_record_finding -> aqi_finish_testcase). Use aqi_snapshot/aqi_screenshot whenever you need to ground a step in the live page. After all: aqi_job_complete.
- testcase-generation: the user wants the stored test-case library created/updated. contextFile carries the resolved per-job instructions (scope, whether to drive the live screen, and the exact on-disk file layout) — follow it. This job WRITES files directly with your editor tools (you do NOT have an MCP tool for this); it produces files, not a live run, so no aqi_emit_testcases / aqi_start_testcase. Surface a short summary via aqi_record_finding, then aqi_job_complete.
- Resuming a finished run: if the user asks for more work on a run you already closed with aqi_job_complete, reuse that SAME runId — aqi_emit_testcases / aqi_start_testcase reopen it automatically. You MUST end every test case with aqi_finish_testcase and the run with aqi_job_complete again; otherwise the test case is left "running" forever and its steps are not attributed.

Comparison flow (comparing two pages/states — old vs new UI, before vs after, two tabs):
- Do NOT read both sides into context and reason over raw data — it is slow, token-heavy, and inaccurate. Use the deterministic offline tools.
- For each surface, extract BOTH sides then compare: aqi_extract_table -> aqi_extract_table (other side) -> aqi_compare. The single aqi_compare tool infers the artifact type (table/form/chart/section/style) from the extracted artifact, so use the same extract+compare pattern for forms, charts, sections, and styles.
- Pass a unique artifactKey to each extract call and reuse those keys (plus a fresh diffArtifactKey) in the matching aqi_compare call. Use the SAME canonical column/field keys on both sides via columnMappings/fieldMappings so columns align even when wording differs.
- aqi_compare runs in Node with NO AI tokens and returns a compact verdict + summary. To surface the full breakdown to the user, call aqi_record_finding with diffArtifactKey set to that diffArtifactKey (and diffSideLabels, e.g. { left: "Old UI", right: "New UI" }) — the manage UI renders the row/cell/point differences in a bottom sheet.
- aqi_get_table_data / aqi_get_form_fields are for inspecting/asserting a SINGLE page only. Never use them to compare two pages — use the extract+compare path.

Assertions: prefer the first-class aqi_assert_* tools (text/value/element_has_class/element_count/style/network_success/no_console_errors, plus aqi_assert_state with state=visible|enabled|checked) over ad-hoc aqi_evaluate. A failed assertion auto-records a fail finding.

Reporting issues you notice (even unrelated ones):
- While working a task or fix, if you notice ANY problem — alignment / spacing / overflow, color-contrast or readability, broken or inconsistent styling, console or network errors, accessibility gaps, confusing copy — record it with aqi_record_finding even when it is unrelated to the current task. Unrelated findings are surfaced for the user but you do NOT fix them; only fix what the task/bug asks for.
- When a finding is about something visible, capture a FOCUSED screenshot of just that element/region (aqi_screenshot with selector or rect) and pass its returned path as screenshotFile so the user sees exactly what you mean. The server copies that screenshot into the run so it is never lost to temp cleanup.
- Set type='warning' (or 'fail') and an appropriate severity for design/contrast/alignment issues; leave isBug=false unless it is a genuine functional defect.

Tool rules:
- aqi_evaluate READS DOM/state only — never act on the page through it. No el.click(), no dispatchEvent (MouseEvent/KeyboardEvent), no setting input.value: synthetic events miss framework handlers and step tracking, so they silently do nothing. Use aqi_click / aqi_type / aqi_hover / aqi_select_option / aqi_drag / aqi_press_key for every mouse/keyboard action. ALWAYS pass a short description (≤ 15 words) of what the script inspects — shown in the live run step row, so "Inspect page" is never acceptable.
- aqi_screenshot writes to disk and returns a path. Capture the SMALLEST useful region: pass a selector or rect to grab just the element/area you care about. Use fullPage:true only when you genuinely need the whole page as its large and slow.
- Findings are tool calls, not prose. If it's not a finding, it does not get surfaced.
